questionnaires.title: Control attestation
questionnaires.summary: A control's owner confirms that it still operates as described, or says what has changed. An attestation is the owner's word. It is not a test.

questions.label: Does this control still operate as its statement describes?
What is different from the statement?
questions.help: Say what is done now, and since when.

questions.label: Is the statement itself still the right description of what should be done?
What should it say?
Is there evidence on record, still in date, that shows it?

options.label: There is, and it is out of date

questions.label: Who will collect it, and by when?
Are you still the right person to answer for this control?
Who should it be?

questionnaires.title: Risk self-assessment
questionnaires.summary: A risk's owner looks at it again: whether it still stands, what has changed, and whether its rating and its plan are still right.

questions.label: Could this still happen here?
Why not?
questions.help: For example: the system was retired, or the work has stopped.

questions.label: Since it was last assessed, what has changed?

options.label: The controls, or how well they work

questions.label: Say what has changed.
Are the controls linked to it working?
Is the residual rating on record still right?
questions.help: If it is not, assess the risk again after answering.

questions.label: Should it be higher or lower, and why?
Is the treatment plan on track?
What is holding it up?

questionnaires.title: Unit completeness check
questionnaires.summary: A unit's steward confirms that what the unit has and depends on is on record, and that the right people are named.

questions.label: Are the unit's processes, systems, third parties, and information all on record?
What is missing?
In the past year, has the unit taken on a system, a supplier, or a body of sensitive data that is not yet on record?
What, and who looks after it?
Is anything on record that the unit no longer has?
What should be retired?
Does every record name an owner who is still here and still the right person?
Which records need a new owner?
Is there something that worries you about the unit's work that is not in the register?
What is it?
questions.help: A sentence is enough. Someone will follow up.

questionnaires.title: System security profile
questionnaires.summary: Whoever runs a system says how it is protected: what it holds, who can reach it, and who patches, backs up, and watches it.

sections.title: What it holds and who can reach it

questions.label: What does the system hold or handle?
Can it be reached from the internet?
About how many people can sign in to it?
How do people sign in?

options.label: With accounts the system keeps itself
With an account that people share

questions.label: Is a second factor required?
Why is no second factor required for everyone?
questions.help: It can be reached from the internet, or it holds sensitive information.

questions.label: When someone leaves, how is their access removed?

options.label: By itself, with their organization account

questions.label: How many people have administrative rights?
Does its maker still supply security updates?
What is the plan for it?
Who applies updates?

options.label: Nobody, as far as I know

questions.label: Is it backed up, and has a restore been tried?

options.label: Backed up, and a restore has been tested
Backed up, and a restore has not been tried
It holds nothing that would need restoring

questions.label: Do its logs go to central security monitoring?

questionnaires.title: Third-party tiering
questionnaires.summary: A few questions about what a third party holds, how it reaches the organization, and what relies on it. The answers set its tier by the program's rules.

questions.label: What is the most sensitive of the organization's information it will hold, receive, or be able to see?
questions.help: Count every service it provides. The classes are the organization's own.

questions.label: Is any of it one of these?

options.label: Identifiable health information, as HIPAA defines it
Data held under another party's terms, such as controlled-access genomic data
Government identifiers, such as Social Security numbers
Student education records, as FERPA defines them

questions.label: About how many people does it hold records about?
questions.help: A breach of health information about 500 or more people must be reported at once, and to the press.

options.label: It holds no records about people

questions.label: How will it reach the organization?

options.label: Administrator or privileged access to the organization's systems
Remote access to the network or to systems
Accounts in the organization's identity system
A connection that sends or receives the organization's data
Unescorted access to laboratories, the clinic, or equipment rooms

questions.label: If it stopped tomorrow, what would happen to the work that relies on it?

options.label: Critical research, care, or operations would stop within a day
Work would slow, and could be kept going another way for weeks
Little: it could be replaced without much trouble

questions.label: Does it pass the organization's information or access on to others it uses?
Is any of the organization's information held or reached from outside the United States?

questionnaires.title: Due diligence: short
questionnaires.summary: Eight questions for a third party with little at stake: how it protects what it holds, and what it does when something goes wrong.

questions.label: Who answers for information security, and how can they be reached?
questions.help: A name or role, and an email address.

questions.label: Which independent reports or certifications cover the service you provide to us?
questions.help: Choose each that is current. You can be asked for a copy.

options.label: A penetration test by an independent firm in the last 12 months

questions.label: Does everyone who can reach our information or systems sign in with a second factor?
Is our information encrypted when it is stored and when it is sent?
Is a person's access removed when they leave, or no longer need it?
Will you tell us of an incident that affects our information within 72 hours of finding it?
At the end of the work, will you return or destroy our information and confirm it in writing?
Is there anything else we should know?

questionnaires.title: Due diligence: standard
questionnaires.summary: A security questionnaire for a third party that holds confidential information or reaches systems.

questions.label: Who answers for information security, and how can they be reached?
questions.help: A name or role, and an email address.

questions.label: Which independent reports or certifications cover the service you provide to us?
questions.help: Choose each that is current. You can be asked for a copy.

options.label: A penetration test by an independent firm in the last 12 months

questions.label: Do you have written information security policies, approved by your leadership and reviewed each year?
Do your staff complete security awareness training when they join and each year?
Are staff who can reach our information checked before they start, as the law allows?
Does everyone who can reach our information or systems sign in with a second factor?
Is administrator access limited to named people, and reviewed at least every quarter?
Is a person's access removed within a day of their leaving, or no longer needing it?
Can our people sign in to your service with our own identity provider?
Is our information encrypted where it is stored?
Is it encrypted whenever it is sent over a network?
Is our information stored and reached only from within the United States?
Where is it stored or reached from, outside the United States?
At the end of the work, will you return or destroy our information and confirm it in writing?
How soon are critical security updates applied to the systems that hold our information?
Are access to our information and changes to your systems logged, and the logs kept at least a year?
Is our information backed up, and is restoring it tested at least once a year?
Do you have an incident response plan, tested in the last year?
Will you tell us of an incident that affects our information within 72 hours of finding it?
Have you had a security incident that had to be reported to customers or regulators in the last three years?
What happened, and what changed afterwards?
Do others you use (subcontractors or cloud providers) hold or reach our information?
Who are they, and what does each do?
Do they agree to terms at least as strict as yours with us?

questionnaires.title: Due diligence: full
questionnaires.summary: The full security questionnaire, for a third party that holds restricted or regulated information or is relied on for critical work.

questions.label: Who answers for information security, and how can they be reached?
questions.help: A name or role, and an email address.

questions.label: Which independent reports or certifications cover the service you provide to us?
questions.help: Choose each that is current. You can be asked for a copy.

options.label: A penetration test by an independent firm in the last 12 months

questions.label: Do you have written information security policies, approved by your leadership and reviewed each year?
Is a named person accountable for information security across your organization?
Do you assess the risks to the information you hold at least once a year?
Do your staff complete security awareness training when they join and each year?
Are staff who can reach our information checked before they start, as the law allows?
Do you carry cyber liability insurance?
Does everyone who can reach our information or systems sign in with a second factor?
Do administrators use a second factor that resists phishing, such as a security key?
Is administrator access limited to named people, and reviewed at least every quarter?
Is everyone's access to our information reviewed at least twice a year?
Is a person's access removed within a day of their leaving, or no longer needing it?
Can our people sign in to your service with our own identity provider?
Will your staff reach our network or systems remotely?
How, and how is that access controlled and recorded?
Is our information encrypted where it is stored, with keys you manage separately from the data?
Is it encrypted whenever it is sent over a network?
Is our information kept apart from other customers' so that none of them can reach it?
Is our information stored and reached only from within the United States?
Where is it stored or reached from, outside the United States?
Is our information used only to provide the service to us, and never to train models or for other customers?
At the end of the work, will you return or destroy our information and confirm it in writing?
Will you create, receive, keep, or send protected health information on our behalf?
Will you sign a business associate agreement with us?
Have you assessed your compliance with the HIPAA Security Rule in the last year?
Is security reviewed as your service is designed and changed, with code reviewed before release?
Has an independent firm tested your service for weaknesses in the last 12 months, and were the serious findings fixed?
Are changes to the systems that hold our information approved and recorded?
How soon are critical security updates applied to the systems that hold our information?
Do you scan those systems for weaknesses at least every month?
Do your computers and servers have protection against malicious software that is kept current?
Are access to our information and changes to your systems logged, and the logs kept at least a year?
Are the logs watched for signs of attack at all hours?
Do you have an incident response plan, tested in the last year?
Will you tell us of an incident that affects our information within 72 hours of finding it?
Have you had a security incident that had to be reported to customers or regulators in the last three years?
What happened, and what changed afterwards?
Is our information backed up to a separate place, and is restoring it tested at least once a year?
Do you have a plan to keep the service running through a disaster, tested in the last year?
How soon could the service be running again after losing its main site?

options.label: Longer, or it is not known

questions.label: Do others you use (subcontractors or cloud providers) hold or reach our information?
Who are they, and what does each do?
Do they agree to terms at least as strict as yours with us?
Do you review their security at least once a year?
Is there anything else we should know?
